newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan envoy urges aid review after diplomatic snub.
newsitem.headline: Japan envoy urges aid review after diplomatic snub.

text.p: A senior Japanese government minister on Thursday urged Japan to review its overseas aid after what he took as a diplomatic snub during a visit to Zimbabwe last week.

Japanese Health Minister Junichiro Koizumi, angered that an appointment with Zimbabwe President Robert Mugabe was not kept during a visit to Harare last week, made the proposal after informing Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto of the incident, Japanese officials said.
An authoritative source told Reuters that Japan planned a formal diplomatic protest to Zimbabwe over the missed appointment.

Koizumi, who was in Harare last week as a special envoy carrying a letter for Mugabe from Hashimoto, became upset after Zimbabwe officials kept him waiting while Mugabe attended another meeting and then failed to show up at an arranged time.

"Japan is now working to cut its official development assistance (ODA) budget by 10 percent. The Foreign Ministry should comprehensively review the indiscriminate distribution of ODA," Koizumi told reporters upon his return to Tokyo on Wednesday.
"I doubt if it (Zimbabwe) has any diplomatic sense," he added.
The Zimbabwe embassy in Tokyo declined to comment on the incident, but the Zimbabwean media reported that officials explained the case as a "misunderstanding" on protocol.
Zimbabwe's newspaper, The Herald, reported on Wednesday that Mugabe intended to meet Koizumi but another meeting he attended lasted longer than scheduled.
The Herald quoted diplomatic sources in Zimbabwe as saying, "The Japanese minister's reaction was highly unusual as it was normal for envoys to wait."
"It would not be normal for a president to drop everything he may be doing in order to to meet an envoy, said one European diplomat," the Herald added.

"There was no intention whatsoever to snub Mr. Koizumi. We made the arrangements for him to meet the President but unfortunately his meeting took a little longer," The Herald quoted a Zimbabwe Foreign Ministry official as saying.
Zimbabwe received nearly 10 billion yen ($86.2 million) in aid from the Japanese government in fiscal year 1995 as loans and grants.
